notes: "He did not tell lies now." reads slightly off; "He did not tell lies anymore." is more natural and still A1.
"He ran away and played all day." is a loose condensation (in the original he runs off and Geppetto is arrested), but acceptable for A1.
"Plant your coins there, and a money tree grows." is a little flat; "Plant your coins there, and a money tree grows overnight." reads better and keeps present simple.
"At home, the Talking Cricket gave him some advice." follows directly after he runs out of the house; "Later, at home, ..." would smooth the jump.
"When the Fairy was sick, he sent her all his money." could be "When he heard that the Fairy was sick, ..." (he is not with her).

issues.quote: He went to sea in a little boat to look for Pinocchio.
issues.problem: Placed after the reunion in a simple past sequence, it reads as if Geppetto went to sea after meeting his son inside the dogfish. It is backstory and needs to be marked as earlier.
issues.fix: He had gone to sea in a little boat to look for Pinocchio, and the dogfish had swallowed him.

issues.quote: "Every week there has six Thursdays and one Sunday, and nobody studies."
issues.problem: Word order is non-native ('there has'); it reads as a calque.
issues.fix: "There, every week has six Thursdays and one Sunday, and nobody studies."

issues.quote: Pinocchio forgot his promise and followed them to an inn.
issues.problem: No promise was made in the B1 text (Fire-Eater just gives coins for Geppetto; Geppetto says 'Now you can go to school'). The reference dangles.
issues.fix: Pinocchio forgot about his poor father and followed them to an inn.

notes: "the cat acted blind" is understandable but "the cat pretended to be blind" is more natural.

"Pinocchio said no twice, but the third time he climbed on the coach." In the original (and in B2/C1) he rides one of the donkeys because the coach is full; "he jumped on a donkey and went with them" would be consistent across levels.

"The fish ate the donkey away, and a wooden puppet swam up again." 'The fish' is not introduced and 'again' is odd; consider "Fish in the sea ate the donkey skin away, and a wooden puppet came up instead."
"Then, although it was the middle of winter, he sold his only coat..." 'he' could be misread as Pinocchio; name Geppetto explicitly.
The ruler who frees the prisoners is an emperor in the original; 'king' is an acceptable simplification (also in C1).
"eating raw fish by the light of a candle": in the original Geppetto lives on the provisions of a swallowed ship; consider "eating the last of his food".
Strong, faithful and genuinely literary (painted fire, nose seized by the policeman, pears, four pennies, thirty-five fish, the asthmatic dogfish, the fox and cat truly lame and blind at the end).
The switch from 'it' (the log) to 'he' (the puppet) works, but the first sentence's 'Long before it learned to walk' is slightly forced; optional.

summary: A1, A2, B2 and C1 are faithful to Collodi, natural and level-appropriate, with correctly keyed quizzes. B1 fails on three concrete points: a backstory sentence about Geppetto going to sea that reads as happening after the reunion, the non-native 'Every week there has six Thursdays', and a dangling reference to a promise never made in that level.
